# Review, pass 1 — secret-history-149-150 (§§149–150)

Reviewer: adversarial pass. Inputs: conventions.md, runbook.md, run3/RUNBOOK.md §2, packet.md, units.json (draft), known-forms.json,
the pilot (register), and the units.json / review.md of earlier parts for house renderings. No modern translation opened or recalled.
All edits made in place by script (original saved outside the repo); `t` was not retyped.

Mechanical checks (all pass after editing): 64 units; `t` equals the packet word for word (491 words, each consumed once, in order,
including the split `mököriġül- | dekün`); one `words` entry per word; `ln` right (149 u0–52, 150 u53–63); `p: true` on u0 and u53 only;
no unit crosses a §. Every word's Ming gloss appears in brackets in its morph glosses except where fixed below.
Unit numbers are 0-based indices into `sentences` (u0 = "Ničügüd-Baγ̇arin-u Širġüġetü …"); word numbers are packet indices.

## Findings refused (with reason)

- **u8–u9 reading of the dilemma** — the draft's logic (I laid hands on my lord; if I do not kill him I am marked and killed; if I kill him I am killed) agrees with the Ming
  (殺了也 / 被殺 我), and its n says it is a guess. No better reading from the grammar and the Ming alone; left.
- **u10 "take a cushion … and die"** — the idiom note is honest and the Ming 墊背 is rendered literally with the inference flagged. Left.
- **u14/u29 "turn back"** — Ming 囘去 / 囘咱 are "return"; the reading "withdraw, do not go home" is the draft's, and flagged. Left.
- **u31 heilügsed / Teden-i** — the draft's reading (the sons separated from the Taichi'ud party) sits awkwardly with u32 ("bringing those men along"). Could not be improved from the Ming; left, the
  tentativeness is already in the n.
- **u41/u47/u52 tebčin jadažu "could not give up"** — the Ming 捨 (… 不能) is rendered literally; the alternative "could not bear (to harm him)" is a guess from Chinese 捨不得 and not adopted; the draft's own n already admits it fits poorly.
- **u44 supplying Chinggis as the asker** — plausible from the context (the answer is to Chinggis, u45); left.
- **u56 alduγsan-dur "lived together"**, **u57–u58 the attachment of in-ü / the killing** — undecidable from the Ming; draft's hedges stand.
- **u58 who killed whom** — the draft's reading (Wang killed his father's younger brothers) fits Gür Qan and his uncle in u59; left, already flagged.
- **u37 position of bida (word 280)** — could close the question or open u38; the Ming gives no help; left with the draft's cut.
- **Shirgügetü, Alaq, Tongqaid, Jaqagambu spellings in `i`** — consistent with earlier parts (Tarqutai-Kiriltuq, Jaqagambu 140-143, γ → q in Tarqutai); left. (Širġüġetü's ġ has no precedent; "Shirgügetü" kept.)
- **Morph lemma quibbles (bosu-, heilü-, aldu-, širγuγ̇ula-, "stem inferred")** — already marked as inferred; left.
- **irge gloss (word 481)** — known-forms has irge as "wether" with "people" as a broadening; that is the glosser's task, not changed here.

## Counts by severity
Major 0 · Moderate 13 · Minor 15 (items 14–29, some grouped) · Trivial 2 (items 30–31).

## Remaining doubts
1. ile- "send" vs "go" (item 9): follows the Ming 敎去着 and the object Tarqutai, but ileġüžei (u25) is read "go away" and the same stem is "lest he go"; one meaning for all is not shown.
2. tebčin jadažu (u41, 47, 52): "could not give up" fits poorly with leaving him; the underlying word may differ.
3. u31–u32: who parted from whom and who was "brought along"; u58–u61: subjects of the Wang/Yesügei/Gür chain are inferred, no names printed.
4. u36 haran / nököčel ügeġün: loose parse, "men without any companions" is the least certain English in the part.
5. u8–u10 and u13–u15, u26–u29: the logic of the three speeches rests on the Ming glosses; the notes say so.
6. Second pass: gloss.json to be checked against the changed morph (mököri- · -ġül- · -de- · -kün; ile-; keġe- · -je; Qān-luγ̇a lemma; Waṅ-Qaγan "Wang Qahan" vs Waṅ-Qān "Wang Qan").


# Review, pass 2 — secret-history-149-150

Second pass, adversarial: units.json re-read after pass 1 (l, i, n, every morph gloss, every Ming bracket against the packet), every
gloss.json entry against the text and the unit morphs. Edits by script (backups outside the repo). Checked mechanically: gloss.json keys equal
novel-forms.json keys exactly (no extra, none missing); every entry's closing Ming bracket equals the novel-forms value (only `dekün`: `[]` written
as `[no Ming gloss]`, kept); each of the 8 `__broaden__` entries is the current glossary entry whole + " · " + the new reading (prefix test passes);
every word's morph brackets compared with the packet's Ming gloss.

## Changes

### Moderate
1. **u3, u34 (words 38, 254) · morph, n** — irežüġüi was analysed ire- + -žü + -ġüi ("is, was, contracted from bui"). The three earlier parts (043-054, 074-079, 125-130)
   and the glossary read -žüġüi as one narrative-past ending. Done: ire- + -žüġüi, n of u3 rewritten; the "contracted bui" claim is gone.
2. **gloss `ögüre`, `ögügšen-ü`; u39, u63 morph** — the entries and morphs took the stem as `ögü-`; the glossary's 40-odd forms (ögüġed, ögüleġe, ügüdkün) all
   lemmatise `ög-` with a linking vowel. Done: morph ög- + -üre, ög- + -ügšen + -ü; entries say "linking vowel ü + …".
3. **u55 (word 427) · morph** — lemma `ireġü-` against the entry's `ire-`. Done: ire- + -ġü- (extension; looks causative, Ming reads plain "come") + -leġei.
4. **u13, u28 · morph, gloss `jakiγ̇užai`, `jakikün`** — morph lemma `ya-` + `-ki-` while the entries' lemma is `jaki-`. Done: morph lemma `jaki-` (gloss keeps "ya- 'what' + ki- 'do'").
5. **gloss `ileġüžei`, `alaγ̇asu`, `surγaγ̇asu`, `jakiγ̇užai`, `jakikün`** — line-pinned persons ("lest he …, I fear he will go", "if (I) kill", "if (I) teach", "what will (you) do?",
   "shall (we)"): a conditional or participle carries no person. Made general: "(one)". 
6. **gloss `itegelten`; u36 morph, n** — "possessive -ten (a variant of -tan/-tü)": -tan is not the possessive (here it is "and others", Najaγ̇a-tan). Done: "read as a variant of

## Refused
- **`tarqutai-kiriltuγ-i` "the Ming 行 is bracketed in one occurrence"** — true of the three occurrences (人名(行) / 人名 行); phrased as a fact about the edition, not pinned to a line. Left.
- **`bidan-i` "inclusive"** — Ming 咱 vs 俺 on `ba` shows the inclusive/exclusive contrast in this very part. Left.
- **Entries `alaγ̇ai` "third-person optative", `ileġüžei` "apprehensive", `jakiγ̇užai` "question"** — each says it is read from the Ming or not explained by it. Left.
- **`ičuγ̇aba`, `hoilažu`, `γardaba`, `seṅterežü`, `sujin`, `sona`, `oi`** — stems inferred from the Ming and so marked; no modern form asserted beyond that. Left.
- **`dekün` "[no Ming gloss]"** — novel-forms has `[]`; the explicit words are clearer to a reader. Left.
- **`itegelten` Ming 中** — kept in the bracket as printed.
- **`irge`** (known entry "wether" + "also people") already broadened in the glossary; no change needed.

Major 0 · Moderate 6 (items 1–6) · Minor 6 (items 7–12) · Trivial 1 (item 13).

## Remaining doubts
1. ile- "send" vs "go" (pass 1 doubt 1) unchanged.
2. -žai in jakiγ̇užai (question) vs ileġüžei (apprehensive): the entries say so; possibly one ending.
3. `tebčin jadažu` "could not give up" still fits poorly with leaving him; may be a different word.
4. -ġü- in ireġüleġei: the Ming says plain "come"; causative not excluded.
5. Which instrumental form follows which sound (-jar / -γ̇ar): left unstated.
